access.title: Face access interactive planner
access.lead: Demo access architecture and a preliminary BOM—for discussion only, not a formal quote.
access.planner_flow: Suggested order: set scale → review list → export or contact.
access.guide_learn: Click a diagram node for device notes; use tabs for Learn / Scenarios / Plan.
access.guide_scenario: Pick a scenario; the diagram highlights the matching path.
access.guide_plan: Adjust inputs on the right; diagram quantity badges update live.
access.event_grant: Architecture point: unlock only after identity/policy approval; the door sensor separately reports whether the door actually opened.
access.event_deny: Architecture point: denied cases issue no normal unlock; the sensor should not show a normal passage open event.
access.event_fire: Architecture point: fire/egress follows approved hardware loops—not face recognition or network alone.
access.consult_hint: Prefills the contact form with the summary. Submission emails the team—it is not a CRM lead ID.
access.role_disclaimer: Illustrative only—not a real customer policy.

face.title: Face terminal
face.desc: Captures a face image and matches identity. Depending on the model, results go to a separate controller or an integrated unit handles part of the control path.
face.note: Confirm recognition distance, backlight, liveness, fallback credentials, and supported interfaces.

controller.title: Access controller
controller.desc: Applies identity, door, and schedule policy, then drives lock, door sensor, and request-to-exit circuits.
controller.note: Controller count follows real door capacity and I/O—never assume one controller per door.

lock.title: Electric lock & door
lock.desc: The lock changes state from an approved control output. An unlock command does not mean the door was opened.
lock.note: Confirm leaf type, single/double doors, current draw, fail-safe/secure behavior, and fire/egress rules.

platform.title: Central management
platform.desc: Holds people, door rights, schedules, and events. YSOP/YSCP integration needs version, license, API, and device checks.
platform.note: One logical suite does not mean one new physical server or every feature in every edition.

power.title: Power & backup
power.desc: Powers readers, controllers, and locks. Some devices use PoE; some locks need dedicated supplies.
power.note: Size power and UPS runtime; choose fail modes per lock—do not apply one rule to every door.

exit.title: Egress & REX
exit.desc: Request-to-exit lets people ask to leave; emergency egress may also need mechanical release.
exit.note: Door type, building use, and code decide egress—two-way face readers do not replace a compliant exit path.

sensor.title: Door contact
sensor.desc: Reports actual open/closed state for forced door, held open, and ajar events with the controller.
sensor.note: A contact shows whether the door is open—not who passed or how many people.

fire.title: Fire linkage
fire.desc: Uses approved fire/egress hardware loops for emergency passage.
fire.note: Emergency release must not rely on front-end JS, a cloud API, or ordinary network alone.

valid.title: Authorized employee passage
valid.desc: Identity, door, and schedule are valid; unlock is issued.
steps: Issue unlock and await door-contact report
valid.label: Granted

unknown.title: Unknown person denied
steps: Log denial if the device supports it
unknown.label: Unknown

door.title: Identity without door rights
door.desc: Enrolled, but not in this door’s allowed groups.
door.label: Wrong door

time.title: Outside authorized hours
time.desc: Identity and door are valid, but not in schedule.
time.label: Wrong time

offline.title: Network down: offline needs validation
offline.desc: Only devices with a valid local cache may grant while the platform is offline.
steps: Unlock only if local rights match
offline.label: Offline

fire.title: Fire linkage: approved safety loop
fire.desc: Emergency egress must not rely on face recognition. Lock and egress design must be pre-approved.
steps: Hardware safety loop acts as designed
fire.label: Fire

permission_reason.no_door: This role has no rights for this door
permission_reason.ok: Matches demo role, door, and schedule

reader.name: Face terminal
reader.note: Demo assumes 1 reader per side; integrated lock control still needs product confirmation.

controller.name: Separate access controller
controller.basis_separate: Based on doors, interfaces, and layout per controller
controller.basis_integrated: Integrated design does not assume a separate controller
controller.note_separate: Do not estimate one controller per door; protocols and secure mounting need confirmation.
controller.note_integrated: If the terminal cannot safely drive locks, a separate controller may still be required.

lock.name: Electric lock set
lock.basis: One single-leaf lock set per door (provisional)
lock.note: Double doors, leaf type, lock style, and fire rules can change quantity.

sensor.name: Door contact
sensor.note: Mounting and leaf structure need a site survey.

exit.name: REX / emergency release
exit.basis: Confirm egress method, REX, mechanical exit, or release per door
exit.note: Two-way face readers do not replace compliant egress.

psu.name: Lock PSU / UPS
psu.basis: Size by voltage, current, zones, and backup time
psu.note: Confirm fail modes and fire linkage; do not treat UPS count as door count.

network.name: PoE switch & networking
network.basis: Ports, PoE budget, and cable distance
network.note: Not every face terminal uses PoE.

platform.name: Central access management
platform.basis: {sites} site(s) demo for {people} users and {doors} doors—capacity still TBD
platform.note: One logical suite ≠ one new server; YSOP/YSCP edition and licensing TBD.

wiring.name: Cabling, conduits, cabinets, install & test
wiring.basis: Measure per door location and existing pathways
wiring.note: Do not infer length or labor from door count alone.

summary.title: YenShow | Preliminary access requirements (not a quote)
summary.core: Core: face access, door/schedule rights, central management
summary.readers_note: Note: demo reader count {readers} assumes 1 per entry side or 2 for both sides; confirm traffic directions.

cctv.title: CCTV architecture & storage
cctv.lead: Switch data paths, inspect devices, and estimate decimal TB from bitrate and retention. The 20% uplift is planning headroom—not RAID purchase capacity.
cctv.diagram_click_hint: Select a device to review its role and data path
cctv.diagram_hint_record: Highlight = recording stream from IPC to NVR
cctv.diagram_hint_live: Highlight = live view and platform pull
cctv.guide_inspect: Switch paths or select a node for notes; use the tab for storage estimates.
cctv.guide_storage: Adjust cameras and bitrate; results are decimal-TB demo estimates.

all.title: CCTV surveillance architecture
all.desc: Cameras capture and encode; switches carry traffic; NVRs record and play back; VMS integrates viewing, devices, and events when the project allows.
points: Separate front-end, network, and back-end roles
Distinguish NVR recording from VMS management
Confirm real platform and device compatibility
all.note: Integrated NVRs, small sites, or cloud designs may differ from this schematic.

record.title: Recording path from IPC to NVR
record.desc: Encoded streams travel from cameras through the switching fabric to the recorder and land on local or validated storage.
points: Confirm average and peak bitrate per camera
Check NVR inbound bandwidth, channels, and bays
Plan retention days and usable space after fault tolerance
record.note: The NVR need not share a cabinet with cameras; switch and uplink design must match distance and traffic.

live.title: Centralized live monitoring
live.desc: A management platform can pull compatible streams and deliver live views to authorized operator clients.
points: Size multi-view decode and bandwidth needs
Scope which cameras each role can see
live.note: Some designs relay via NVR; others pull from IPC—do not assume one path before selection.

remote.title: Secure remote viewing
remote.desc: When policy and network controls allow, authorized users may view video through protected access paths.
points: Prefer VPN or protected proxy/access layers
Assess uplink bandwidth and audit logs
remote.note: Do not expose NVR management ports to the public internet. Remote designs need security and product validation.

ipc.title: IP camera
ipc.desc: Turns sensor input into encoded network streams, optionally with night vision, WDR, or smart events.
points: Power, IP rating, and site conditions
ipc.note: Megapixels alone are not enough; field of view and target pixel density matter.

poe.title: PoE switch
poe.desc: Switches Ethernet for multiple devices and, when compatible, powers IPCs over the same cable.
poe.note: Account for real PoE budgets; not every camera should assume PoE.

core.title: Core network
core.desc: Aggregates edge switches, NVR, and VMS traffic over copper or fiber depending on scale.
core.note: Shared uplinks need total bitrate and failover traffic sized carefully.

nvr.title: NVR recorder
nvr.desc: Receives IPC streams and manages recording and playback within model channel and capacity limits.
points: Supported camera count and inbound bandwidth
nvr.note: RAID is not a backup; off-site retention for critical video needs a separate plan.

vms.title: VMS platform
vms.desc: Centrally manages devices, sites, events, and users according to licensing and integration scope.
vms.note: YSOP / YSCP interest still depends on shipping versions, licenses, and compatibility tests.

client.title: Operator client
client.desc: Authorized local or remote workstations use VMS or NVR live view and playback.
client.note: Never share admin passwords publicly. Controlled remote access is not the same as exposing management ports.
